claims.statement: Upstream OAI.AtomicTriangular.universal_energy_minimum (openai/math, AI-generated, Comparator-accepted, not peer reviewed): for every g with AdmissiblePotential g and every C with LocallyFinite C and DensityOne C, latticeEnergy g <= energy g C and latticeEnergy g = energy g A. Certifies the statement about upstream's definitions only.

TriangularRiesz.riesz_admissible (s > 0: t^(-s/2) is admissible) and TriangularRiesz.latticeEnergy_riesz_lt_top (s > 2: latticeEnergy (riesz s) < top). Prior published work doi:10.5281/zenodo.23285631.

TriangularDensity.universal_any_density and triangular_optimal_any_density (D2, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23285631): for rho > 0 and admissible h, (sqrt rho)^-1 A is locally finite, has DensityRho rho, and minimises energy h among locally finite DensityRho-rho configurations.

AutoresearchYukawa.admissible_mul (products of admissible potentials are admissible, pointwise Leibniz sign lemma mul_sign), admissible_congr (admissibility depends only on values on (0, inf)), phi_admissible (kappa > 0: exp(-kappa sqrt t) is admissible).

AutoresearchYukawa.yukawa_admissible and triangular_yukawa_optimal: for kappa > 0, g kappa t = exp(-kappa sqrt t)/sqrt t is AdmissiblePotential, hence latticeEnergy (g kappa) <= energy (g kappa) C for every locally finite density-one C.
AutoresearchYukawa.latticeEnergy_yukawa_lt_top: for kappa > 0, latticeEnergy (g kappa) < top (via g <= (2/kappa^2) t^(-3/2)), so YK-A-0005 is not top <= top.

Negative control AutoresearchYukawa.c_not_admissible: exp(-kappa sqrt t) cos t is not admissible (negative at t = pi), so admissibility is not vacuously satisfied. The theorem does not apply to it; this does not show that triangular optimality fails for it.
AutoresearchYukawaMix.admissible_add, admissible_smul (c >= 0), admissible_zero, admissible_sum (finite nonnegative combinations): upstream's AdmissiblePotential is closed under these operations.

AutoresearchYukawaMix.g_rescale (pointwise, t > 0: g kappa (t/rho) = sqrt rho * g (kappa/sqrt rho) t), yukawa_optimal_any_density and latticeEnergy_yukawa_rho_lt_top: at every density rho > 0 the rescaled triangular lattice minimises the planar Yukawa energy among locally finite density-rho configurations, with finite minimum.

AutoresearchYukawaMix.yukawaMix_admissible, triangular_yukawaMix_optimal, latticeEnergy_yukawaMix_lt_top, yukawaMix_optimal_any_density, latticeEnergy_yukawaMix_rho_lt_top: every finite mixture sum_i w_i exp(-kappa_i r)/r with w_i >= 0, kappa_i > 0 is admissible, minimised by the triangular lattice at density one and (rescaled) at every density, with finite minimum.

Negative control AutoresearchYukawaMix.signedMix_not_admissible: g_1 - 2 g_2 is not admissible (value 2e^-1(e^(1/2) - 2) < 0 at t = 1/4). So the admissibility lemma yukawaMix_admissible needs the sign condition on the weights, and the optimality theorem does not apply to g_1 - 2 g_2. This does not show that triangular optimality fails for it.
CKMRV Definition 1.3: universal optimality is minimising p-energy for every completely monotonic function of squared distance; density is bookkeeping (rescaling by rho^(-1/d)).
CKMRV Section 1: a lattice has p-energy sum_{x in Lambda minus 0} p(|x|) (no factor 1/2), assuming absolute convergence.

CKMRV footnote 2: if p is completely monotonic on (0, inf) then so is r -> p(r^(1/2)); more generally if p and q' are completely monotonic then so is p o q (each term of the k-th derivative has sign (-1)^k).

Upstream manuscript (OpenAI, Universal optimality of the triangular lattice, 2026-09-23), Section 1: the theorem permits singular potentials and divergent lattice sums, and identifies the minimum value, not all minimizers.

CKMRV Section 1 (arXiv:1902.05438 version, p. 8, remark after Theorem 1.4): uniqueness of the minimiser cannot hold among all configurations, because removing a single particle changes neither the density nor the energy (so a lattice with a vacancy has the same energy).

Human demonstration (paper Section 3): t^(-1/2) and exp(-kappa sqrt t) are completely monotone on (0, inf); Leibniz gives closure under products; e^x >= x^2/2 gives g <= (2/kappa^2) t^(-3/2) and a convergent lattice sum; sums and nonnegative multiples preserve the sign pattern; rescaling t -> t/rho preserves it. A prose proof, not machine-checked; it mirrors the Lean proofs of YK-A-0004..0011 step by step.

Physics reading: g kappa (r^2) = exp(-kappa r)/r is the planar Yukawa (3D-screened Coulomb) pair interaction between particles confined to a plane, with kappa in units of the inverse density-one length; it is not the 2D Debye-Hueckel Green function K0(kappa r). Upstream latticeEnergy and diskEnergy count ordered pairs (no 1/2), so they are twice the per-particle energies of the numerics. The theorem is classical (T = 0), concerns the liminf disk-averaged energy, and fixes the minimum value, not the minimiser. Novelty is formal only: complete monotonicity of the Yukawa potential in r^2 and the convex-cone/product closure of completely monotone functions are classical.

Hugging Face search (2026-10-25, public, unauthenticated) for dusty plasma, complex plasma, colloid, colloidal, yukawa and wigner crystal found no particle-position dataset of a dusty plasma or colloid (absence by search, not proof); OC20 (colabfit/OC20_IS2RES_val_id) supplies disordered initial conditions, not physics.

Exact (untruncated) lattice energies per particle, (1/2) sum, density one: kappa=1 tri 1.625321339606275 square 1.634855495317198; kappa=2 tri 0.39354284893239105 square 0.40097424876505744. Exact minus published shifted-force (r_c = 8): 0.01771212 (kappa=1 tri), 9.482107e-06 (kappa=2 tri). Square-minus-triangular gap changes by -2.2e-06 (kappa=1) and -3.235e-09 (kappa=2). Consistency evidence only.

Positive controls: independent 40-digit mpmath direct sum and Ewald splitting agree with the Rust f64 values to at most 1.66e-16 (threshold 1e-9); Rust direct vs Ewald and image-summed box vs lattice sum agree to the 1e-15/1e-16 level.

Negative controls: published shifted-force lattice energies fail the 1e-9 test against the exact ones by the erratum amount; the square lattice in a 17x17 box under the exact potential has 72 (kappa=2) and 64 (kappa=1) negative Hessian modes and relaxes to an energy above e_tri.

Relaxed comparison: 24 relaxed stages from 21 published seeds re-relaxed under the exact potential with CVODE; 0 fall below the exact triangular energy beyond f64 resolution (below_exact_floor is exact_gap < 0 with zero tolerance; 1 stage(s) sit at exact_gap = 0.0, the perfect lattice, within f64 noise: the perfect lattice in the kappa=1 box differs from the lattice sum by -2.2e-16); no negative Hessian modes; gaps change by at most 5.3e-7 (kappa=1) and about 1e-10 (kappa=2). A subset (11 of 50 stages at kappa=1, 13 of 100 at kappa=2); annealing not re-run.

The dataset card at that revision (data/oc20_card.json) gives the dataset DOI 10.60732/b4005525 and the journal DOI 10.1021/acscatal.0c04525.

Sampled sign checks (mpmath, 40 digits): (-1)^n g_1^(n) > 0 at orders 0..6 on 159 points of t in [0.05, 4] (figures/fig_signs.json); (-1)^n g^(n) >= 0 at orders 0..8 on t = k/20, k = 1..80, for g_1 + 0.5 g_3 and its rho = 3 rescaling (contribution/numeric_gate_mix.json); g_1 - 2 g_2 violates the pattern (value -0.2585 at t = 1/4). Exploration only.
